content.body:
The development of even-thicker armor on enemy tanks had been foreseen by German gun developers as the war got underway, and a gun bigger than the 50 mm PaK 38 was already in demand by the German High Command. What resulted was an anti-tank gun that was based so much around the earlier excellent PaK 38 that not only was it visually similar, but also small for its caliber.
In every way it was an outstanding gun being small, easy to handle for a "heavy" gun, having a low profile and incorporating a number of innovative design features. And the gun had higher penetration performance than either of the excellent 75 mm guns in service on the German AFV's of the time. The crew was protected from small arms and machinegun fire by a double-layered shield.
The PaK 40 is a big step up from the PaK 38, and only an 88 firing late-war ammunition is going to better it, unless you consider the ultimate 75 mm "long" fitted to the famous Panther tanks. It is a very accurate gun, allowing you to aim quickly and with some confidence if the relatively high recoil forces offset your original shot solution after firing. A lot of tanks are not going to require a second impact however, unless you're dealing with a heavily armored late campaign Churchill VII or a very bad shot angle. As usual, if you have a bad impact angle on the front of an enemy tank, you probably have a better impact angle on the thinner side armor. Try hitting it there instead.
content.brief: TYPE: Heavy Anti-Tank Gun CALIBER: 75 mm MUZZLE VELOCITY: 793 m/s EFFECTIVE RANGE: 2,000 m WEIGHT: 1,486 kg TOWING CLASS: Heavy
content.title: PanzerabwehrKanone (PaK) 40 AT Gun
